title: Retail Sales Performance Report: 2023–2024
executive_summary: Across 520 orders, the business generated $445,325 in total revenue over 2023–2024. Revenue grew 10.1% year-over-year, driven by a strong second half of 2024. The East region led all regions. High-discount electronics represent a notable revenue concentration risk, and a single customer accounts for 6.2% of total revenue.

key_findings.statement: The business recorded 520 orders totalling $445,325.09 in revenue, yielding an average order value of $856.39.
East led all regions with $130,516.69 in revenue, followed by North ($124,845.75), West ($99,428.16), and South ($90,534.49). East outpaced South by $39,982.20.

2024 quarterly revenue accelerated through Q3 then eased slightly: Q3 was the peak at $71,674.99, followed by Q4 ($68,948.71), Q2 ($56,616.79), and Q1 ($36,108.31). Revenue nearly doubled from Q1 to Q3.
Revenue increased year-over-year: 2023 revenue was $211,976.29 and 2024 revenue was $233,348.80, a gain of $21,372.51 or approximately 10.1%.
22 Electronics orders carried a discount of 20% or more, generating $50,035.33 in combined revenue — an average of approximately $2,274.33 per high-discount order.

Order revenue is highly right-skewed: the mean is $856.39 but the median is only $313.28, with a standard deviation of $1,295.74. Values range from $5.27 to $7,844.02, indicating a long tail of large orders pulling the mean upward.
There are 222 unique customers. The single highest-revenue customer contributed $27,793.13, representing 6.2% of total revenue — a meaningful concentration for one account.

limitations: The dataset covers only two calendar years (2023–2024); longer historical data would be needed to assess whether the 10.1% YoY growth is a sustained trend or an anomaly.
Customer identifiers are anonymised, so it is not possible to assess churn, repeat-purchase behaviour, or the business risk posed by the top customer without additional CRM data.
High-discount Electronics analysis uses a fixed 20% threshold; the business impact of discounts just below this threshold is not captured.
Regional labels (North, South, East, West) are not mapped to specific geographies, limiting actionability of regional findings.
The order revenue distribution analysis does not distinguish between product categories, which may have very different price and margin profiles.
conclusion: The retail business delivered solid growth in 2023–2024, with total revenue of $445,325 and a 10.1% year-over-year increase. The East region and the second half of 2024 were the primary growth drivers. However, the highly skewed order distribution, notable customer concentration (one customer at 6.2% of revenue), and significant high-discount Electronics activity warrant attention to protect margin and reduce dependency risk going forward.
